_about: Part 4 entity-resolution rules, reconstructed from part4_methodology.md and checked against part4_answer_key_map.csv (the original Part 4 output, 4,256 rows, 1,038 entities). Used by part4_entities.py. Regexes are Python, applied case-insensitively.

1_name_key.description: Lowercase Benchmark_Name, split into runs of letters/digits, drop the filler words, join with no separator.

2_cec_year_key.description: Any 'CEC <year>' phrasing, either word order, collapses the whole name to cec_<year>. Only whitespace or a hyphen may separate CEC and the year (CEC'2013 and CEC'13 are NOT matched, as in the original). Different years stay distinct.

3_blocking.description: Rows sharing (Category, name_key) form one base entity. Base entity ids are assigned in order of first appearance.
3_blocking.never_a_key_fallback: A Benchmark_Name in never_a_key is not used as a grouping key; such a row gets its own entity per paper (key 'unkeyed:<Paper_ID root>', resolution_method 'no_benchmark_name'). New for v2; the original data had no such rows.

4_acronym_merge.description: Within one Category, a name ending in a parenthesised acronym whose letters are the initials of the preceding words is merged with the same name without the acronym. The side with more rows keeps its entity id (ties: the earlier id); the absorbed rows get resolution_method 'name_key+acronym_merge'.

5_text_hash_dedupe.description: part4a: rows are deduplicated by sha256(matching_text) for description building; this does not change the grouping (blocking works per row). Reported as a count only.

6_suite_child_split.description: Only inside cec_<year> groups (the only keys that merge different names). Names containing a range are suite-level and stay in the suite (range-exclusion fix). A name with exactly one function number becomes a single_function child keyed by that number. A name listing two or more function numbers (no range) becomes a named_subset. A CEC transformation configuration (Bias/Shift/Rotation with a 3-digit code) becomes a named_subset keyed by its code. The parent keeps entity_type 'suite' only if it has children; children are numbered after the base ids, groups in descending row count, children by first appearance.
6_suite_child_split.series_split_flag: --series-split (off for the fidelity run, on for v2)

series_split_series.description: MSTSP<n> and RWMOP<n> are already one entity per number under the base rules (their names differ). With --series-split they are tagged with a series_key so they can be read as one series; no rows are regrouped and no empty parent entity is created.

7_digit_guard.description: Report-only. Inside one final entity, two DISTINCT single-function names (each carrying exactly one series identifier, same letter prefix, different number, no range) would be a digit merge (DTLZ1 vs DTLZ2, G2 vs G4). Ranges folding into their suite and spelling variants of one function (F01 vs F1: same number) are not reported. Every case goes to digit_merge_report.csv.

8_post_part4_repairs.description: Repairs applied after Part 4 in the old pipeline (all in one initial commit, so git history gives no order; the order below follows the scripts' docstrings: Part 5 build -> enrichment (part7_apply_enrichment.py) -> entity_dedup_audit.py -> find_true_duplicates.py -> merge_tsp_duplicates.py -> fix_underspecified_entities.py). On v2 they are applied by rule, not by old entity id.

spelling_variant_merges.description: Within one Category, the entity holding the absorbed name_key is merged into the entity holding the target name_key. Old pipeline: done on entity records after Part 5 (the target kept its description); v2: done on the map before Part 5, so the description covers every member.

underspecified_descriptions.description: Same Category, identical base_description, not a parent/child pair, not a numbered variant (names equal after digit stripping) or named-instance variant (names equal after stripping a trailing ' on/for/-/(' clause), and name word Jaccard < 0.4 -> prepend canonical_name to base_description. On the old data this selects exactly the 7 hard-coded ids.

extraction_artifacts.description: Old pipeline dropped E00599 (Benchmark_Name 'Evolutionary Algorithm', 1 row) from problem_entities.json but kept it in the map. v2 keeps every row in an entity and flags such an entity 'extraction_artifact_suspect' instead of dropping it.
